purpose: Discovery and provenance registry for historical Mobile Bay Jubilee event evidence. Discovery is not ingestion; each source must be normalized into event_evidence before calibration use.

sources.title: Sporadic Mass Shoreward Migrations of Demersal Fish and Crustaceans in Mobile Bay, Alabama
sources.author: H. Loesch
sources.use: historical event dates, seasonality, location, timing, wind/rain/tide hypotheses
sources.guardrail: Recover primary table/text before creating individual event rows.

sources.title: Extensive oxygen depletion in Mobile Bay, Alabama
sources.author: E. B. May
sources.use: dated spatial DO observations and nearshore contact-strip physics
sources.guardrail: Hypoxia observations are not automatically Jubilee events.

sources.title: The Jubilee phenomenon
sources.author: T. Lowery
sources.use: historical mechanism/location synthesis and cited event sources

sources.title: Effects of Coastal Upwelling and Downwelling on Hydrographic Variability and Dissolved Oxygen in Mobile Bay
sources.use: wind-driven shelf/bay exchange, DO and hydrographic response; 2016 CTD/survey calibration
sources.guardrail: Scientific process/calibration source, not direct Jubilee label unless paper documents one.

sources.title: Something that only happens in two places in the world just occurred in Mobile Bay
sources.social_evidence: Embedded first-person @tiffofthesouth post states Jubilee that morning with fish, crab, shrimp and stingrays along shore.

sources.title: Mobile Bay Experiences First Jubilee of the Summer
sources.social_evidence: Photo credited to Explore the Eastern Shore/Facebook; report identifies flounder, shrimp and blue crabs in shallows near Point Clear.
sources.use: event label; source chain to original Facebook evidence

sources.title: Mobile Baykeeper 2018 Annual Report
sources.use: historical Point Clear and Battles Wharf water-quality monitoring coverage; not Jubilee labels

sources.title: State of Mobile Bay 2008
sources.use: historic NCA bottom dissolved-oxygen condition and Jubilee mechanism context

sources.title: Why Do Fish Flood the Shore in Mobile Bay?
sources.use: historical detection-sign hypotheses: quiet conditions, fish popping, nighttime human notification/search behavior
sources.guardrail: Use for hypothesis generation/detection context, not dated event labels without corroboration.
Do not archive private/copyrighted media without permission; preserve factual structured observations and provenance.
